- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 30d horizon.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior 7d high), model frequently overshoots in next 7–14d; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.  
- If true outcome shows rapid decline after a peak, model often fails to capture early drop; adjust forecast to reflect 3–5d lag in price correction.  
- For 30d horizon, if history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model tends to underestimate; apply upward bias to counteract mean reversion bias.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative values (e.g., -0.33 or 0.00), model often underperforms; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
